Developer guide

Material for the maintainers of libhdrgrading: the API reference generated from the public headers, how to build every configuration, how changes are verified, the conventions the code follows, and a map of the source tree.

API referenceEvery function, type and constant of the eight public headers (hdrgrading.h, video.h, gpu.h, metadata.h, sidedata.h, plugin.h, filter.h, codec.h), with the headers' own comments, cross-linked. Generated from include/hdrgrading/*.h.
BuildingDependencies, CMake presets and options, GPU toolchains (Dawn, Tint), FFmpeg, WebAssembly, installing and using the library.
Testing and verificationThe test suites, the three verification tiers, the parallelism from free memory, CI and the determinism levels.
ConventionsThe C style (checked by scripts/check_style.py), memory, determinism, the public API, shaders, SIMD, the presets' evaluation and CLAUDE.md.
Source treeWhich directory and file holds what.
Maintaining this manualHow this manual is generated and how to change its pages and diagrams.

Ground rules

  • The library is not finished: backward compatibility is not kept, and the plugin ABI stays at version 1 until it is frozen.
  • When files or names change, CLAUDE.md (the file structure) is updated with them.
  • The output is deterministic and that is tested: a change that makes the output depend on the thread count, the FP environment or the run is a bug (Conventions).

The user-facing Architecture and Analysis, plan, apply pages explain how the library is put together; CONTRIBUTING.md has the development environment and the dependencies.
